p.t: Core rule: exclude recent buyers from retargeting
Exclude customers who completed a purchase in the last 30 days, so no budget goes to showing ads to recent
buyers.
Exclude people who purchased in the last 30 days from the remarketing audience. Once they buy, showing ads for the products they already bought wastes spend.
Build a 30-day purchase audience and exclude it from remarketing ads. This keeps remarketing focused on people who have not yet bought from you.
Always exclude purchasers from retargeting audiences, and check that the exclusion is set up before the campaign starts. Retargeting people who have already bought annoys them and wastes ad spend.
The sources give two windows: 30 days for Google Display remarketing and 180 days for Meta and TikTok.

Use the window listed for the platform you are running.

TikTok tends to repeatedly show ads to people who already bought, which hurts performance. Buyers from the last 180 days must therefore be excluded manually from prospecting campaigns.
When testing MOF retargeting audiences, exclude the BOF audiences.
p.h: BOF and buyer exclusions during MOF retargeting tests

p.t: Remove buyers from every retargeting ad set. Keep buyers in retargeting only when promoting a new product or a special offer to them.
Leaving buyers inside retargeting ad sets wastes budget on people who already purchased, unless the ad promotes a new product or special offer.
Time-based remarketing audiences in Google Ads
1. Create separate remarketing audiences by time period: 7-day, 14-day, 30-day, and so on.
2. In each audience, exclude users from the shorter time periods to prevent overlap.
3. Example: the 14-day audience excludes users from the 7-day audience. The 30-day audience excludes users from both the 14-day and the 7-day audiences.
4. This prevents the same user from seeing ads in multiple time-based remarketing audiences.
Disable Optimized Targeting in the audience segment configuration.
Leaving it enabled is a critical error because it prevents proper audience precision.
Always turn off optimized targeting in remarketing campaigns. When it is left on, Google may show the ad to audiences outside the remarketing list.
Targeting expansion must be switched off for retargeting ad groups.
Otherwise the platform can reach cold users who never visited the site, so only the chosen retargeting audience should see the ads.
Leaving the option that lets Meta reach people beyond the custom audience turned on broadens the ads to anyone Meta predicts will buy.
This defeats a remarketing campaign, which should only reach people who already visited the site.
1. Go to Display campaigns and open the remarketing campaign.
p.h: Adding audience exclusions in Google Ads

p.t: 2. Open Audiences, keywords, and content, then click Audiences.
3. Click show table to see the audience segments. A new audience shows as not eligible while it is under review.

4. Scroll to the bottom to the Exclusions section and click edit exclusions.
5. Search for the purchasers audience (people who bought in the last 30 days) and select it.
6. Click save and check that the exclusion appears in the list below the targeted audience.
An audience exclusion cannot be added while the campaign is being created. Add it after the campaign exists, under the campaign's Audiences section and its Exclusions tab.
Negative keywords
Remarketing campaigns should remain wide open with minimal negative keywords. Only exclude audiences of recent purchasers.
Do not limit remarketing by keywords or other filters, because everyone who visits your site is a potential repeat customer. (2023.)
Remarketing does not use negative keywords. Its targeting is based on audiences, so the setup only needs recent website visitors and the exclusion of recent customers. (2023.)
The two 2023 sources differ on whether any negative keywords are used: minimal ones according to, none according to. Both agree that keyword or other filters should not narrow remarketing.
Retargeting usually does not need narrowing by location beyond the target country, or by demographics,

because the people in the audience have already visited the store.
Automatic placements are the default choice for these campaigns.
1. Open Audience Manager and create a website visitors audience: any page visited, matching the URL.
p.h: Audiences for visitors who did not convert

p.t: 2. Exclude visitors of a page with the thank you text, which is the Shopify order confirmation page.

3. Combine the two into a single audience. An optional time window of up to 60 days can be set.
Formula:
Combined audience = all website visitors (any page, matching the URL) minus visitors to a page containing the thank you text
The thank you page is the Shopify order confirmation page, which usually includes the thank you text unless it has been changed.
The time frame can be extended to 60 days.
Remarketing audiences should exclude customers, so people who just bought are not shown ads asking them to complete an order.
Exclusions for buyers are applied automatically when the audience uses the non-purchaser setting.
